Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most urgent first. Your records run up to mid-October 2026.

1. Your stool test (FIT) on 4 November 2025 was positive. Your records show no colonoscopy or other follow-up test since then. A positive stool test needs a colonoscopy to look at the bowel. Ask your doctor whether you still need one and how to book it. If you had it done somewhere else, it would not show in these records.

2. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol was 131 mg/dL in February 2025, above the usual target of 99. Atorvastatin was prescribed two days later, and there is no cholesterol test on record since then. Ask whether you need a repeat lipid test to see how the statin is working.

3. Your last HbA1c (blood sugar average) was 6.9% in February 2026, about eight months ago, and no test is recorded since. People with diabetes usually have this every three to six months. Ask when your next one is due.

4. Your records show no urine albumin test, which checks for early kidney damage. Your eGFR (kidney filtration) was 69 in February 2026. People with type 2 diabetes usually need this urine test every year. Ask about it.

5. Your records show metformin ended in April 2024, and Jardiance was prescribed in February 2025. No diabetes medicine is listed in between, and your HbA1c rose from 7.4% to 8.3% over that time. This may be a gap in the records, but it is worth asking about.

6. No vaccines are recorded at all. Ask your doctor which ones you are due. For someone your age with diabetes this usually includes a shingles vaccine, a pneumonia vaccine, and a yearly flu shot.

Nothing is outstanding from the July 2025 chest scan: it showed no pulmonary embolism (blood clot in the lung), even though a blood test (D-dimer) was raised, and the chest wall pain that prompted it has resolved.

checkup.answer:
Yes, there are several things to raise. The most important is your stool test. Your fecal immunochemical test (FIT) on 4 November 2025 was positive. A positive FIT means you need a diagnostic colonoscopy to find the cause. Nothing in your records up to 15 October 2026 shows that this was done or booked. If it happened somewhere else, make sure your doctor has the result. If not, book it now.

Your diabetes checks look overdue. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, about eight and a half months ago. Your metformin is marked as ended on 15 April 2024, and the records give no reason. Empagliflozin (Jardiance) was prescribed on 20 February 2025. Ask whether you are taking it and what your diabetes plan is now. Your A1c peaked at 8.3% in January 2025 and has come down since.

Your cholesterol was high on 18 February 2025 (LDL 131 mg/dL). That test was done two days before atorvastatin was prescribed, and there is no repeat cholesterol test in your records.

Your kidney function is still in the normal range (eGFR 69 in February 2026, down from 73 a year earlier). I do not see a urine albumin test in the past year, which is usually part of yearly diabetes care. I also do not see a diabetic eye exam. These may have been done elsewhere.

One item that looks like a problem but is not: your pulmonary embolism entry is marked as ruled out, and the CT scan on 8 July 2025 showed no PE. You may still want to ask about the high D-dimer blood test from that day.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most important first. The records I have run to 15 October 2026, so anything done at another clinic or after that date will not show here. Please check these points with your doctor.

1. Your stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025 came back positive. I cannot find a colonoscopy or any other bowel follow-up after it. A positive result normally leads to a colonoscopy, so this is the most urgent item. If that has not happened, call the office before your appointment.

2. Metformin was stopped on 15 April 2024, and the records give no reason. Your next diabetes medicine, empagliflozin (Jardiance), was not started until 20 February 2025. Over that gap your A1c (a blood sugar average over about three months) rose from 6.7% to 8.3%. Ask why metformin was stopped and whether you went without diabetes treatment.

3. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026. That is more than eight months ago. With diabetes it is usually checked at least every six months, so it is due.

4. Cholesterol: in February 2025 your LDL was 131 and your total cholesterol was 212, both high. You started atorvastatin on 20 February 2025. No cholesterol test has been recorded since, so a recheck is probably due.

5. Kidneys: your eGFR (a kidney filtering number) was 69 in February 2026, down from 73 a year earlier. That is still above the usual cut-off of 60. No urine albumin test appears anywhere in the records. People with diabetes normally have one every year.

6. Blood count: none appears in the records. Since your stool test was positive, ask whether a blood count should be checked for anemia, which can come from slow bleeding.

7. Blood pressure: no reading appears anywhere in these records. Ask for one at the check-up.

8. Your condition list still includes pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung). The CT scan in July 2025 found no clot, and the entry is marked as refuted. Ask your doctor to confirm it is not a current diagnosis and to correct the list.

9. Diabetes checks: I see no eye exam (retinal or dilated) and no foot exam recorded. Both are usually done every year for diabetes.

The records may be incomplete, for example if other clinics ran tests, so treat this as a list of questions for your doctor rather than a diagnosis.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most urgent first. Your records run from February 2024 to a download dated 15 October 2026, so anything after that is not something I can see.

1. Your stool test in November 2025 was positive. I cannot find a colonoscopy or other look at the bowel after it. A positive stool test normally needs a colonoscopy to find the cause, and that result is now nearly a year old. Please ask about this first.

2. Your diabetes control. Your last HbA1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026. It peaked at 8.3% in January 2025 and has come down since. There is no HbA1c on file after February. Checks are usually every 3 to 6 months, so one is due now.

3. Your diabetes medicines do not line up in the records. Metformin is marked as finished on 15 April 2024. The next diabetes medicine on file is Jardiance (empagliflozin), prescribed on 20 February 2025. Your HbA1c kept rising during that gap. Please confirm which diabetes medicines you take now, and whether metformin was stopped on purpose.

4. Cholesterol. Your LDL was 131 mg/dL (high) on 18 February 2025. Atorvastatin 20 mg was prescribed two days later. I cannot find any cholesterol test since then. A recheck is normally done a few weeks to 3 months after starting a statin.

5. The lung clot scare in July 2025 was ruled out. A CT scan showed no pulmonary embolism, and the clot entry is marked as refuted, which is correct. Your D-dimer blood test was raised that day, and I cannot find a repeat test. Ask that the clot is not kept as a real diagnosis, and ask whether the raised D-dimer needs anything further.

6. Your kidney function is in the normal range. eGFR was 69 on 16 February 2026 (60 or above is normal), and creatinine and potassium were normal. This matters for Jardiance and metformin, so it is worth checking each year.

7. I cannot find a urine albumin test anywhere in your records. It is the yearly kidney check for people with diabetes. It may simply not be in these files, so ask whether it has been done.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I'd raise, most important first.

1. Your stool test (FIT) on 4 Nov 2025 was POSITIVE, and I can find nothing after it: no colonoscopy, no referral, no repeat. A positive FIT needs a colonoscopy, ideally within a few months, and it is now about a year. This is the main thing to bring up.

2. Diabetes monitoring is due. Your A1c has come down well (8.3% in Jan 2025, 7.6, 7.1, then 6.9% in Feb 2026), but the last one is over 8 months old and these are usually checked every 3-6 months. Kidney tests in Feb 2026 were normal (creatinine 0.88, eGFR 69, though eGFR has drifted down from 73). I see no urine albumin test, eye exam or foot exam in the records.

3. Cholesterol has not been rechecked. Your last lipid panel (Feb 2025) had LDL 131 and total 212, both high. Atorvastatin 20 mg was recorded on 20 Feb 2025, just after, so you should have a repeat panel to see whether it is working.

4. Medicines: you take Jardiance and atorvastatin. Metformin was stopped in April 2024. Ask whether that was intended and confirm your list is right.

5. No vaccines are recorded at all (flu, COVID, pneumonia, shingles, RSV, tetanus). At 69 several are recommended. This may just be missing records, so bring any you have had elsewhere.

6. For reassurance: the July 2025 chest pain visit was worked up with a CT scan showing no pulmonary embolism, and the chest wall pain resolved. The scan noted mild spine wear, which is common. Nothing is needed there.

I also see no records of breast cancer screening (mammogram) or bone density, which may simply be held elsewhere.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most urgent first. These come from your records and general medical knowledge. Your records may not include tests or visits done somewhere else, so check before assuming something was missed.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill). The hospital told you to stop it on March 5, 2026, after your sodium fell to 123. But your clinic and pharmacy records still list it as active, you reported taking it on May 14, 2026, and your sodium was low again on June 15, 2026 (134). Please call Dr. Marsh's office soon, tell them whether you are still taking it, and ask them to recheck your sodium. If you have dizziness, confusion, a fall, or feel very unwell, get care the same day.

2. Thyroid test overdue. In March your TSH was high (7.9) with a normal free T4. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I see no repeat test in your records.

3. Lung nodule. The CT of October 18, 2025 found a 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung and recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ends around mid-October 2026, and I see no chest CT or other follow-up. The discharge instructions from that visit did not mention it.

4. Kidney stone follow-up. The 4 mm stone was still listed as active. The discharge instructions said to see urology if it had not passed in 2 weeks. I see no record that it passed, no urology visit, and no repeat urine test after the large amount of blood seen in your urine then.

5. Cholesterol and statin. Your September 2025 LDL was 142 and HDL was 48. You have type 2 diabetes, and no statin appears in any record. There has been no cholesterol test since. Ask whether a statin is right for you.

6. Kidney urine test for diabetes. Your kidney filtration (eGFR 71) is normal. However, I see no urine albumin test (UACR) since your diabetes diagnosis. It is usually done once a year.

7. Vaccines. Your first Shingrix dose was given on November 8, 2025. The second dose is due 2 to 6 months later, and I see none. No flu shot for the 2026-27 season is recorded yet. No tetanus booster appears anywhere in your records. Check whether you had these somewhere else.

8. Medication list cleanup. Lisinopril, which was stopped in 2025 because of cough, still shows as active in one older export. Amlodipine, losartan, metformin and Claritin each appear several times from different sources. Ask for a full medication review.

9. Screening. I see no mammogram in the last two years and no cervical screening in the last five years. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, and the next is due around 2029.

10. Good news. Your A1c has come down from 6.9% to 6.6%, and your eye exam in May 2026 showed no diabetic eye damage.

The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so that window closed around October 18, 2026. Nothing after that visit mentions the spot or a scan.

4. Cholesterol and a statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, total cholesterol 221, HDL 48 (low), and triglycerides 155. You were diagnosed with type 2 diabetes that month, and guidelines usually recommend a statin for people with diabetes your age. No statin is on any of your lists, and there has been no cholesterol test since September 2025.

5. Vaccines. The second Shingrix dose is not recorded. It was due 2 to 6 months after the first on November 8, 2025. No flu shot for this season is recorded, and I see no Tdap or COVID vaccine anywhere. Prevnar 20 from the same visit is complete. Fernhill's vaccine list also leaves out the November 2025 shots.

Your eye exam on May 14, 2026 found no diabetic eye damage, and the next is due in May 2027. Ask whether you went to the diabetes education visit suggested in September 2025. Mammogram and cervical screening also do not appear in these records, though they may have been done elsewhere. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, so the next is due around 2029.

7. The kidney stone follow-up. The emergency department asked you to see your primary doctor within a week, and urology if the stone had not passed in two weeks. Nothing in your records shows either visit or a repeat urine test. Ask whether a repeat urine test is needed to confirm the blood in your urine has cleared.

Its problem list has no low sodium entry. Please ask Fernhill to add these and to get the hospital and emergency summaries.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I'd raise at your check-up, most important first.

1. Lung nodule follow-up looks overdue. The CT you had for the kidney stone in October 2025 found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so by now (about 12 months) it is due or past due. I found no chest CT or other follow-up in your records. You've never smoked, which is reassuring, but the follow-up scan is still advised.

2. Thyroid test not repeated. During your March 2026 hospital stay your TSH was mildly high (7.9) with a normal free T4. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. Your June 2026 labs did not include them, and I found no repeat anywhere.

3. Hydrochlorothiazide: does it add up? The hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 because it caused dangerously low sodium (123). Yet a pharmacy record and the clinic lists still show it as active, and a May 2026 list you reported yourself includes it. Your sodium on June 15 was still slightly low (134). Please confirm with your doctor and pharmacy that you are not taking it, and ask whether the low sodium needs a recheck.

4. Shingles vaccine dose 2. You had the first Shingrix on November 8, 2025. The second dose is due 2 to 6 months later, and I see no record of it.

5. Flu shot. Your last was November 2025, so this season's is due now. No 2026 dose is recorded.

6. Diabetes care. Your A1c has improved (6.9, 6.7, 6.6%) but is still above the usual goal of about 7 or lower only if you're near it. Your eye exam in May 2026 was clear, with the next one due May 2027. I found no urine albumin test (a kidney check recommended yearly in diabetes), no foot exam, and no record of the diabetes education you were referred to.

7. Cholesterol. In September 2025 your LDL was 142 and HDL 48, and you aren't on a cholesterol medicine. At 57 with diabetes, a statin is generally recommended, and the lipids haven't been rechecked. Worth discussing.

8. Kidney stone follow-up. You were told to see your doctor in 1 week and urology if the stone hadn't passed in 2 weeks. I see no record of either, or of whether it passed. Your urine also showed blood then.

9. Cancer screening. Your colonoscopy in 2019 was normal, so the next is due around 2029. I see no mammogram or cervical screening in these records, so check whether they're up to date elsewhere.

10. Record tidy-up. Lisinopril (stopped for cough) still shows as active in an older hospital export, and amlodipine, losartan and metformin appear several times. Your aspirin allergy (hives) and lisinopril cough should stay on file.

The records don't tell me what you're actually taking now or tests done outside these providers, so confirm those with your doctor.

Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most important first.

1. Lung nodule follow-up looks missed. The CT you had for the kidney stone on October 18, 2025 also found a 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist advised a chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so the window ran from about April to October 2026 and has now closed. I can't find a chest CT or any mention of the nodule afterward. You've never smoked, which is reassuring, but this still needs to be scheduled or at least discussed soon.

2. Hydrochlorothiazide may still be on your list. You were hospitalized in March 2026 with a sodium of 123 and a fall, and the water pill hydrochlorothiazide was stopped. But the eye clinic's May 2026 list shows it as something you take, and your June 2026 sodium was still slightly low at 134. Please confirm with your doctor whether you are taking it. If you aren't, the lists need correcting. If you are, that needs attention. It would also be sensible to record it as a drug that caused you a problem.

3. The thyroid recheck wasn't done. Your TSH was high (7.9) during the hospital stay, and they asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6 to 8 weeks later (by about late April 2026). I find no repeat, including in June when you had other blood tests. Free T4 was normal at the time. Illness can raise TSH temporarily, but it needs rechecking.

4. Diabetes care has gaps. Your A1c is 6.6%, improved from 6.9%, and your eye exam in May 2026 showed no retinopathy (next one due May 2027). I find no urine albumin test (kidney check), no foot exam, and no record of the diabetes education referral being completed.

5. Cholesterol hasn't been followed up. In September 2025 your LDL was 142 and HDL 48. With diabetes at your age, a cholesterol-lowering medicine is usually discussed, and no one has recorded that or rechecked your levels.

6. Vaccines. You had flu, pneumococcal (Prevnar 20) and the first Shingrix on November 8, 2025. The second Shingrix dose (due 2 to 6 months after the first) isn't recorded, and this season's flu shot isn't recorded yet. checkup.answer:
Priya, going through your records, these are the things I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ). In March 2026 you were in Kestrel Harbor Hospital for three days with a sodium of 123, dizziness and a fall. The hospital blamed the HCTZ and told you to stop it. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026 (90 days, 2 refills left) and still lists it as active. You told the eye clinic in May that you take it, and Dr. Marsh's June 2026 list still shows it as a current daily medicine. The records can't tell me whether you are actually still taking it. Please check your pill bottles, and ask Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy to cancel it if it was meant to be stopped.

2. Your sodium was still a little low in June 2026 (134, normal is 135 to 145), about three months after the hospital stay. I can't say why. Continuing the HCTZ is one possibility, but nothing in the records settles it. A repeat blood test is reasonable.

3. A lung nodule that needs a repeat scan. The CT you had in the ER for the kidney stone on October 18, 2025 found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ran from April to October 18, 2026, and I see no chest CT in your records. The nodule isn't on any problem list, and the ER discharge instructions never mention it. You've never smoked, which is reassuring, but this follow-up scan is now due or overdue. Please raise it first.

4. Thyroid retest. In the hospital your TSH was high (7.9) with a normal free T4. The discharge note asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I find no repeat in your records. A TSH can be temporarily high during an illness, so a repeat is how you find out if it matters.

5. Your regular clinic's chart looks incomplete. Fernhill Family Clinic's records through June 2026 don't mention the March hospital stay, the low sodium, the kidney stone, or the lung nodule. I see no visit after the hospital stay (you were told to follow up in 1 to 2 weeks) or after the ER visit (1 week). Nothing shows the kidney stone passing or a urology visit. Bring the hospital and ER papers so Dr. Marsh has the full picture.

6. Diabetes care gaps. Your A1c has improved (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6% in June 2026) and your June 2026 dilated eye exam showed no diabetic eye damage, which is good. But your LDL cholesterol was 142 in September 2025 (total 221, HDL 48, triglycerides 155) and I see no cholesterol medicine and no repeat lipid test. I also see no urine albumin test, no foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask whether a statin is right for you, and about these checks. Your next A1c is around December 2026, six months after the June visit.

7. Vaccines. On November 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Shingrix dose 1, and Prevnar 20 (pneumococcal, which is complete). Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first, so it was due between January and May 2026. I find no second dose. I also see no flu shot for this fall, though my records end in July 2026. Fernhill's vaccine list still shows only the October 2024 flu shot, so tell them about the pharmacy shots.

8. Allergy lists don't match. The cough you had on lisinopril (September 2025) is only on Fernhill's list, not on the hospital's, the pharmacy's, or the eye clinic's. If HCTZ did cause the low sodium, it should be recorded as an adverse reaction too. The hospital's early records call your aspirin reaction mild, but its later records call it moderate. Ask to have these made consistent.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years, so it is not due until about 2029. I see no mammogram or cervical screening results in these records. They may simply be held elsewhere, so check when you last had them.

This is not medical advice to change any medicine on your own. Confirm what you are taking with your doctor or pharmacist.

checkup.answer:
Your records run only to mid-July 2026, so anything since then is not visible to me. Here is what I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide may still be in your routine. In March 2026 you were in the hospital for 3 days with a sodium of 123, and the discharge papers say to STOP hydrochlorothiazide because it was the likely cause. The hospital record shows it discontinued on March 5. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2 for 90 days and still shows it active with 2 refills left. Your family clinic's June 2026 summary also still lists it as a current medicine, and does not mention the hyponatremia. Your sodium on June 15 was low again at 134. Please check whether you are taking it. If you are, tell Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy right away. If you are not, ask for the pharmacy and clinic lists to be corrected. The reaction should also be added to your allergy and intolerance list, as lisinopril's cough already is.

2. The lung nodule has not been followed up. The CT done in the ER on October 18, 2025 (for the kidney stone) found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ended around October 18, 2026, and I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule in your clinic notes or problem list. You have never smoked, which lowers the risk, but this follow-up is due now.

3. The thyroid recheck is missing. Your TSH was high (7.9) on March 3, 2026 with a normal free T4 (1.0). The hospital asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I see no repeat. Low sodium can also be linked to an underactive thyroid, so this matters for item 1 too.

4. Vaccines. Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first. You had dose 1 at the pharmacy on November 8, 2025, and I find no dose 2. Your last flu shot on record was that same day, so the 2026-27 shot is not recorded yet. I also find no hepatitis B vaccine, which is generally advised for adults with diabetes under 60, and no Tdap or COVID shots. Those may simply be recorded elsewhere. Your pneumococcal (Prevnar 20) shot is done.

5. Cholesterol and statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, HDL 48 and triglycerides 155. No statin appears on any medication list and no repeat lipid panel appears. Adults aged 40 to 75 with diabetes are generally offered a statin, so ask whether you should start one.

6. Diabetes checks. Your A1c has come down well, 6.9 to 6.7 to 6.6 in June 2026, and your dilated eye exam in May 2026 showed no retinopathy (next due May 2027). I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, no documented foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask about all three. Your next A1c is due around December 2026, when Dr. Marsh asked to see you.

7. Kidney stone follow-up. The ER asked for a primary-care visit within a week and urology if the stone had not passed in 2 weeks. I find no record of either, nor any note on whether the stone passed. It is also absent from your clinic problem list.

8. Details that do not match across records. The aspirin reaction is described as mild in two early 2025 hospital summaries and as moderate in later ones. The lisinopril cough appears in the clinic's allergy list but not the hospital's. Worth asking everyone to align them. Because aspirin gives you hives, you were also kept off ibuprofen and ketorolac in the ER, so ask your doctor about NSAID safety.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal with a 10-year repeat, so it is not due until about 2029. I find no mammogram or cervical screening in any of these records, so ask when they were last done.

checkup.answer:
Your records come from six places (Kestrel Harbor Hospital, Fernhill Family Clinic, Saltmarsh ED, Northbay Labs, Clearwater Eye and Alder Street Pharmacy), and they stop in mid-July 2026. Anything done since then, or done somewhere that isn't in them, won't show up here. Here is what I would raise, most important first.

1. A lung nodule that was never followed up (most urgent). The CT you had in the Saltmarsh ER on Oct 18, 2025 for the kidney stone also picked up a 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6-12 months, so the window ran from April to Oct 18, 2026 and has now closed. I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule anywhere else. Most nodules like this are harmless, and you have never smoked, which lowers the risk. It still needs that scan, so ask for it now.

2. Hydrochlorothiazide: the records disagree about whether you should be taking it. You were admitted to Kestrel Harbor on March 2, 2026 with dizziness, a fall and a sodium of 123. The hospital blamed hydrochlorothiazide and told you to stop it on March 5. But Alder Street Pharmacy filled it on April 2 (90 days, 2 refills left, still marked active), you told the eye clinic on May 14 that you take it, and Fernhill's June 2026 list still shows it as active. Your sodium was low again (134) on June 15. The pharmacy did not refill it on June 28 the way it did your other pills, so you may have stopped. The records can't tell me. Please tell Dr. Marsh exactly what you are taking, and don't start or stop anything on the strength of this note alone.

3. A thyroid recheck that was asked for and not done. Your TSH was mildly high (7.9) during the March stay, with a normal free T4. The discharge instructions asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6-8 weeks, which would have been around late April. I see no repeat.

4. Fernhill doesn't seem to know about your outside care. Dr. Marsh's problem list (June 2026) shows hay fever, high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. It doesn't show the kidney stone, the lung nodule or the March hospital stay. The ER asked you to see your primary care doctor within a week, and the hospital asked for a visit within 1-2 weeks. I find no visit or note about either. Nothing records whether the stone passed or whether you saw urology. It's worth bringing the discharge papers.

5. Cholesterol. Your LDL was 142 and HDL 48 in Sept 2025, and it has not been rechecked. You have diabetes, and you are 57. Guidelines generally advise a statin for people aged 40-75 with diabetes. No statin appears on any of your medication lists and no discussion of one is recorded. Ask whether one is right for you.

6. Diabetes checks that aren't in the records. Your A1c is improving (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6) and your June 2026 kidney function was normal. But I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, which is recommended yearly for people with diabetes, and no foot exam. You were referred to diabetes education in Sept 2025, but nothing shows you went. (The ER urine dipstick showed no protein, but that isn't the same test.)

7. Vaccines. On Nov 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Prevnar 20 and the first Shingrix. The second Shingrix dose is normally due 2-6 months after the first, and none is recorded. No flu shot is recorded since November 2025, so this season's dose may be due. I also find no record of tetanus (Td/Tdap), COVID or hepatitis B vaccines, which are commonly advised for adults with diabetes. These may simply have been given somewhere else.

8. Women's cancer screening. I see no mammogram and no cervical screening (Pap or HPV test) anywhere. These are often done at outside centers, so they may exist. If you can't find them, ask about getting them, since you turn 58 on Nov 4.

9. Allergy lists don't match. Fernhill lists lisinopril (dry cough) as an intolerance, but the hospital, ER, pharmacy and eye clinic lists show only aspirin. The hospital's own medication list says lisinopril was stopped for cough. Also, your aspirin reaction was recorded as mild in April 2025 and as moderate from May 2025 on. Ask each place to update its list.

10. Things that look on track. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years (2029). Your dilated eye exam on May 14, 2026 showed no diabetic retinopathy, and the eye clinic wants you back in 12 months. Your blood pressure on June 15, 2026 was 128/80, which Dr. Marsh called at goal.

This is a review of your paperwork, not a diagnosis. Dr. Marsh can sort out what applies to you.

items.says: Your pharmacy has no lisinopril on file and has been filling losartan, most recently on June 28, 2026.
items.why: The pharmacy's record, through July 14, 2026, lists losartan, metformin, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide and an old tamsulosin course, and nothing for lisinopril.

facts.says: Pharmacy record: losartan potassium 50 mg, first filled September 23, 2025, last filled June 28, 2026 (90 days), active.
facts.name: losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet

absences.what: Any lisinopril prescription or fill after it was stopped on September 22, 2025
absences.coverage: Pharmacy record of medications and fills from September 23, 2025 to July 14, 2026

items.says: Lisinopril and losartan shouldn't be taken together.
items.why: Both lower blood pressure by acting on the same hormone system. Combining them raises the risk of high potassium and kidney problems, so only one of them is used.

facts.says: Your current blood pressure medicine is losartan 50 mg daily, which replaced lisinopril.
facts.name: losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet

knowledge.says: Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system, with an ACE inhibitor plus an ARB, increases hyperkalemia, low blood pressure and kidney injury without added benefit in most people.
knowledge.guideline: ACC/AHA hypertension guideline advises against combining an ACE inhibitor and an ARB.

items.says: Separate from lisinopril: hydrochlorothiazide was stopped in hospital in March 2026 for low sodium, but your clinic and pharmacy still show it as active.
items.why: The hospital stopped hydrochlorothiazide on March 5, 2026 after a sodium of 123. The pharmacy then filled it on April 2, 2026, and your sodium was 134 (low) on June 15, 2026. Someone should confirm what you are meant to take.

facts.says: Hospital medication list: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, STOP taking this medicine, discontinued March 5, 2026 (hyponatremia).
facts.name: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 MG Oral Capsule

facts.says: Pharmacy record: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg last filled April 2, 2026 (90 days), 2 refills remaining, active.
facts.name: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 MG Oral Capsule

facts.says: Clinic medication list in June 2026 still shows hydrochlorothiazide as active from December 9, 2025.
facts.name: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 MG Oral Capsule

facts.says: Sodium 134 mmol/L (low) on June 15, 2026.
facts.name: Sodium

knowledge.says: Thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide can cause low sodium. A hospital stop after an admission for low sodium should normally stand unless the prescriber deliberately restarts it. The records don't show such a restart, and I can't tell whether you are actually taking it.

links.says: The hospital stop on March 5, 2026 is contradicted by a later pharmacy fill of the same medicine.
Continued hydrochlorothiazide could be linked to the still-low sodium in June 2026.
The older 'active' prescription entry was superseded when lisinopril was stopped in September 2025.
The hospital's discontinuation agrees with the clinic's record of the stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2026-03-10T08:15:44Z

Discharge instructions, March 5, 2026.
You were admitted with dizziness and a low sodium level (123). Your sodium improved after hydrochlorothiazide was stopped and with fluid restriction.
STOP taking hydrochlorothiazide. Continue losartan 50 mg once daily, amlodipine 5 mg once daily and metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal.
Follow up with your primary care provider, Elena Marsh, MD, at Fernhill Family Clinic within 1-2 weeks.
Your thyroid test (TSH) was mildly high during your stay. Please have TSH and free T4 repeated in 6-8 weeks, once you have recovered.

Discharge instructions, March 5, 2026.
You were admitted with dizziness and a low sodium level (123). Your sodium improved after hydrochlorothiazide was stopped and with fluid restriction.
STOP taking hydrochlorothiazide. Continue losartan 50 mg once daily, amlodipine 5 mg once daily and metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal.
Follow up with your primary care provider, Elena Marsh, MD, at Fernhill Family Clinic within 1-2 weeks.
Your thyroid test (TSH) was mildly high during your stay. Please have TSH and free T4 repeated in 6-8 weeks, once you have recovered.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.
